title: George Orwell: The Throat of Truth
dek: The writer who survived a bullet through the throat and gave power a name.
mortality_event: Shot through the throat by a sniper in the Spanish Civil War in 1937; survived to write Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four before dying of tuberculosis in 1950.
citation_passage: George Orwell (1903–1950), the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair, was an English novelist, essayist, and critic. In 1937 he fought as a Republican volunteer in the Spanish Civil War and survived a bullet wound to the throat. His account of Spain, Homage to Catalonia, appeared in 1938. Animal Farm followed in 1945, and Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949. He completed the latter while his health worsened, and died of tuberculosis in January 1950. This seven-page biographical comic follows the throat injury and the later writing, connecting his experience of political violence with his continuing attention to power and language.
